evidence: Article URL (nature.com/articles/s44277-024-00006-9) resolves to DOI 10.1038/s44277-024-00006-9, which is the exact DOI of paper 196 (Pagliaccio 2024, NPP—Digital Psychiatry and Neuroscience, "Probing the digital exposome: associations of social media use patterns with youth mental health"). The article IS the paper's journal page.

Title refers to "passive social network usage and depression/negative emotions with envy as a mediator" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-023-37185-y). No ABCD Study connection; not in corpus. Provisional paper 8 (Nagata 2025 JAMA Network Open, ABCD depressive symptoms) does not match — different journal, different authors, different cohort.

Title: "Dynamics of adolescents' smartphone use and well-being are positive but ephemeral" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-022-05291-y). Not an ABCD Study paper; entirely different cohort and study design. Provisional paper 8 (Nagata JAMA Network Open ABCD) does not match.

Title: "Frontoparietal functional connectivity moderates the link between time spent on social media and subsequent negative affect in daily life" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-023-46040-z). Not an ABCD Study paper — uses a different cohort/daily diary design. Provisional paper 8 (Nagata ABCD) does not match.

Title: "Association of screen time with ADHD symptoms and their development: the mediating role of brain structure" (Translational Psychiatry DOI s41398-025-03672-1). Provisional paper_ids 18, 381, 420, 443, 84 — none share this DOI. This is an ABCD screen time/ADHD/brain structure paper not among the 69 included papers.

Article URL (nature.com/articles/s41598-024-63566-y) resolves to DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-63566-y, which is the exact DOI of paper 192 (Nivins 2024, Scientific Reports, "Long-term impact of digital media on brain development in children"). The article IS the paper's journal page.

Title: "Neural correlates differ between crystallized and fluid intelligence in adolescents" (Translational Psychiatry DOI s41398-025-03467-4). ABCD-based neural/cognitive paper but not in the 69 included papers; no phone/SM variable in the title. Provisional paper_ids 18, 295, 381, 443, 57 — none match this DOI.

Title: "Cognitive processing speed and accuracy are intrinsically different in genetic architecture and brain phenotypes" (Nature Communications DOI s41467-024-52222-8). Genetic/cognitive architecture paper, no phone/SM variable; not in corpus. Provisional paper 18 (Li 2024 Advanced Science) does not match.

Title: "Investigating grey matter volumetric trajectories through the lifespan at the individual level" (Nature Communications DOI s41467-024-50305-0). Lifespan grey matter trajectories paper; no phone/SM content; not in corpus. Provisional paper 35 (Shi 2025 Obesity, social media/binge eating) does not match.

Title: "Associations between digital media use and brain surface structural measures in preschool-aged children" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-022-20922-0). Preschool-aged sample — not ABCD Study (which starts at age 9-10). Provisional paper 57 (Lin 2020 J Abnormal Child Psych, ABCD network analysis) does not match.

Title: "Excessive screen time is associated with mental health problems in US children and adolescents: physical activity and sleep as parallel mediators" (npj-Humanities DOI s41599-026-06609-1). Not among the 69 included papers. Provisional paper_ids 139, 157, 158, 393, 394, 398, 84 — none match this DOI. Appears to be a non-ABCD or meta-analytic study.

Title: "Association between ocular diseases and screen time and sedentary time derived from job-exposure matrices" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-024-74854-y). Ocular disease / job-exposure matrix study — not ABCD, not in corpus. Provisional paper 84 (Shou 2026 Acta Psychologica, ABCD cognitive function) does not match.

Title: "Associations between screen viewing at 2 and 3.5 years and drawing ability at 3.5 years among children from the French nationwide Elfe birth cohort" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-023-50767-0). French Elfe birth cohort, preschool age — not ABCD. Provisional papers 295, 84 do not match.

Title: "Heavy screen users are the heaviest among 10,000 children" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-019-46971-6). Likely an early ABCD baseline BMI/screen time paper, but DOI does not match any of the 69 included papers (paper 302 Nagata 2021 Pediatric Obesity has a different DOI). Not in corpus.

Article URL (nature.com/articles/s41598-022-11341-2) resolves to DOI 10.1038/s41598-022-11341-2, which is the exact DOI of paper 190 (Sauce 2022, Scientific Reports, "The impact of digital media on children's intelligence while controlling for genetic differences in cognition and socioeconomic background"). The article IS the paper's journal page.

Title: "The impact of sleep, physical activity and sedentary behaviour on symptoms of depression and anxiety before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in a sample of South African participants" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-021-02021-8). South African sample — not ABCD. Provisional paper 84 does not match.

Title: "Sex-dependent effects of early life sensory overstimulation on later life behavioral function in rats" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-024-78928-9). Rat animal study — not ABCD, not in corpus. Provisional paper 133 (Nagata 2023 OCD screen time) does not match.

Title: "Reciprocal relationship among perceived sleep quality, smartphone overdependence, and depression in Korean adolescents: a cross-lagged analysis using national big data" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-025-33361-4). Korean national big data cohort — not ABCD. Provisional paper 136 (Zink 2024 J Adolescent Health, ABCD sleep/screen time) does not match.

Title: "Late evening room light and sleep restriction reduces the ability of bright morning light to phase advance adolescents' circadian clocks" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-026-37985-y). Circadian biology / room light study — no phone/SM content, not in corpus. Provisional papers 139, 157 (Nagata bedtime screen use / sleep) do not match.

Title: "Passively sensing smartphone use in teens with rates of use by sex and across operating systems" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-024-68467-8). Likely ABCD-adjacent methodological paper on passive smartphone sensing, but DOI does not match paper 154 (Alexander 2025 Psychiatry Research) or any other of the 69 included papers. Provisional paper_ids 154, 177, 314, 420 — none match this DOI.

Title: "Effects of COVID-19 pandemic on incidence of asthma exacerbation in an urban population" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-026-41311-x). Asthma incidence study — unrelated to phone/SM, not ABCD, not in corpus. Provisional paper 177 (Kiss 2023 Health Psychology, ABCD COVID screen time/sleep) does not match.

Title: "The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on neurobiological functioning in adolescents" (Translational Psychiatry DOI s41398-025-03485-2). ABCD-based COVID/neurobiology paper but no phone/SM variable; not among the 69 included papers. Provisional paper 177 (Kiss 2023 Health Psychology) does not match.

Title: "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on incidence of psychiatric disorders using nationwide cohort data and ARIMA models" (Scientific Reports DOI s41598-025-12479-5). Nationwide cohort with ARIMA time-series modeling — not ABCD. Provisional paper 177 (Kiss 2023, ABCD COVID screen time/sleep) does not match.

Title: "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on incident diagnoses in German refugee centres 2018 to 2023" (Nature Communications DOI s41467-025-61876-x). German refugee centre data — not ABCD, not in corpus. Provisional paper 177 does not match.

Title: "Accelerated brain ageing during the COVID-19 pandemic" (Nature Communications DOI s41467-025-61033-4). COVID/brain ageing paper — no phone/SM content, not in the 69 included papers. Provisional paper 177 (Kiss 2023 Health Psychology, ABCD COVID screen time/sleep) does not match.
